newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani businessmen to join anti-tax strike.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani businessmen to join anti-tax strike.

text.p: The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) said on Thursday it had called for a protest strike against the government's harsh IMF-inspired economic stabilisation package.
FPCCI secretary general Rafiq Khan said the strike would take place on Saturday, coinciding with a separate strike called by an opposition alliance led by the Pakistan Muslim League.
On Tuesday Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government devalued the rupee 7.86 percent against the dollar and imposed new tax measures and spending cuts for 1996/97 (July-June).
"These steps are not in the interest of the businessmen or the people because they will increase the cost of production and burden everyone beyond their capacity," Khan told Reuters.
He said the package, designed to persuade the International Monetary Fund to resume payments of a stalled $600 million standby loan, would make local industry uncompetitive abroad.
